title: Change in component count from deleting an edge
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $e$ be an edge of $G$. Writing $c(H)$ for the number of connected components of a graph $H$, and $G - e$ for the graph obtained from $G$ by removing the edge $e$ (keeping all vertices), one has
\[
c(G) \;\le\; c(G - e) \;\le\; c(G) + 1 .
\]
That is, deleting a single edge either leaves the number of connected components unchanged or increases it by exactly one.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
e is an edge of G (e ∈ G.edgeSet)
